findings.evidence: features/006-insights-skill/006-insights-skill-prd.md:R6 + R11 + R12 — R6 specifies two trigger paths (manual `/insights` + scheduled cron), R11 specifies replace-in-place on the active monthly report at `admin/insights/{YYYY-MM}-report.md` with append-only runs.jsonl, R12 specifies cross-month rollover. The interview's Round 6 resolution names replace-in-place explicitly (line 109 of `006-insights-skill-interview.md`). But the PRD does not specify what happens when the two trigger paths fire CONCURRENTLY on the same calendar month: e.g. a scheduled cron auto-fires on the 1st of the month at 06:00 UTC AND the user simultaneously invokes `/insights` from a different terminal session before the cron-invoked run's report write completes. R11's replace-in-place semantic makes this race MORE dangerous than `specflow:complete`'s race (which the 003-PRD's da-r1-f1 caught and resolved with R14's lock-file pattern): both paths could (a) read the same corpus state, (b) compute the same clusters, (c) interactively ask the user to accept/reject proposals (interactive Q&A is asynchronous from the user's perspective; the cron-invoked path doesn't have an interactive surface but does have a write loop that competes with the manual path's user-prompt loop), (d) write divergent reports interleavingly with file-system semantics that aren't atomic at the markdown-content level. The result would be either two runs.jsonl entries with overlapping timestamps (fine — append-only handles it) OR a partially-written report.md (the cron path overwrites mid-way through the manual path's user-prompt loop, the manual path then overwrites with stale-corpus-but-fresh-prompts content). The 003-PRD established the lock-file pattern at `admin/scratch/complete-{task-id}.lock` for this exact failure mode; this PRD inherits the convention via the precedent but does not name a per-month lock-file or in-flight marker.
findings.claim: Cross-artefact ambiguity (concurrency coverage gap) — R6's dual-trigger-path contract (manual + cron) creates exactly the cross-artefact ambiguity DA fires on, and R11's replace-in-place semantic makes the race MORE dangerous than `specflow:complete`'s because both paths could produce divergent reports interleavingly. The Phase 1 + Phase 3 precedent for soft mutual-exclusion is the per-task scratch lock-file pattern (`admin/scratch/complete-{task-id}.lock` from 003-PRD R14); this PRD inherits the convention via the precedent but does not name a per-month lock-file or in-flight marker that would let path B detect path A's in-flight monthly run before both write.
findings.proposed_change: Add a new requirement R15 covering the concurrent-trigger case for the monthly run granularity: 'R15. Concurrent-trigger guard between manual and cron paths. When a scheduled cron invocation is in flight AND the user concurrently invokes `/insights` manually (or vice versa) for the same calendar month, the second invocation detects the in-flight run via a per-month lock file at `admin/scratch/insights-{YYYY-MM}.lock` (created by whichever path starts first; removed atomically on every exit path — successful write, refused exit, schema drift exit, threshold exit). The second invocation refuses with the literal sentinel chat line: "`/insights` for `{YYYY-MM}` is in flight (started `{timestamp}`). Wait for it to complete, then re-invoke if you have additions." Lock files older than 60 minutes are considered stale and ignored (covers crashed-orchestration cleanup AND extended interactive accept-edit-reject sessions; cluster detection itself is fast but R8's user prompts can extend a run's duration; 60 minutes covers a typical interactive monthly run with margin). Stale-lock-detected paths overwrite the lock and proceed.' Add a corresponding AC-15 verifying the lock-file create/remove discipline AND the stale-lock heuristic AND the concurrent-trigger refusal sentinel chat line. The 60-minute threshold is calibrated longer than `specflow:complete`'s 30-minute threshold because /insights's interactive surface is longer (potentially many promotion proposals to walk through). This closes the TOCTOU window the dual-trigger-path contract leaves open and makes the dual-trigger-path contract honest about concurrent invocations — the goal's surface (d) (zero silent failures) requires the race to surface explicitly rather than producing silent corruption.
